purpose: Factual authoring scope for independently written Chemistry practice. These are editorial descriptions and constraints, not copied IB questions or official markschemes.
guideVersion: Published February 2023; updated May 2023 and March 2024. Verified through the official 2027 examiner instructions, which still link the 2026-hosted file.
labelPolicy: SL means shared content available to SL and HL students. Additional HL means content reserved for HL. The updated guide uses HL in place of the former AHL term; the bank keeps ahl as an internal differentiator.
corrections: Hydroxy is the functional-group name; hydroxyl refers to the radical.
Chromatography in S1.1 is not restricted to paper.
S3.2 naming includes numeric prefixes mono, di, tri, tetra, penta and hexa.

assessment.calculator: Permitted on all papers at SL and HL.
assessment.reference: A clean Chemistry data booklet is available on all papers.
assessment.paper1A: One mark per multiple-choice item; no negative marking.
assessment.marking: Question-specific analytic schemes. The bank uses M/A/R labels as its own instructional allocation and must not claim they reproduce an official IB scheme. Correct alternatives and appropriate error-carried-forward credit should be stated where relevant.

constantsAndConventions.atomicMasses: Use values to two decimal places, or supply values explicitly.
constantsAndConventions.units: Reaction enthalpy/Gibbs kJ mol^-1; entropy J K^-1 mol^-1; concentrations mol dm^-3.
constantsAndConventions.source: IB-authored Chemistry data booklet, first assessment 2025, sections 2 and 4, inspected via public mirror.

topics.title: Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
slConcepts: elements, compounds and mixtures; physical separation
particle models of states and changes of state
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Chromatography includes more than paper chromatography.

topics.title: The nuclear atom
slConcepts: nuclear notation and subatomic particle counts for atoms and ions
isotopes, physical differences, weighted relative mass and isotope abundance
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Instrument operating details are excluded.
Isotope abundance calculations without mass spectra are SL.

topics.title: Electron configurations
slConcepts: emission spectra and qualitative photon energy
hydrogen transitions ending at levels 1, 2 and 3
shell capacities, sublevels, s and p orbital shapes
electron configurations and orbital boxes to Z=36, including Cr/Cu exceptions
additionalHlConcepts: ionization energy from convergence frequency or wavelength
successive ionization energy and electron configuration
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Hydrogen spectral series names are not assessed.
Do not mark all electron-configuration questions HL; this is primarily shared material.

topics.title: Counting particles by mass: The mole
slConcepts: amount of substance and particle number
mass percentage, empirical and molecular formulas
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Use data-booklet relative atomic masses to two decimal places.
Relative atomic/formula masses have no unit; molar mass uses g mol^-1.

topics.title: Ideal gases
slConcepts: qualitative non-ideal behavior at high pressure or low temperature
gas-state graphs, molar volume, PV=nRT and combined gas relation
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: No mathematical real-gas model is assessed.
Gas-law names are not assessed.
Use SI pressure and volume with R in J K^-1 mol^-1.

topics.title: The ionic model
slConcepts: ionic formulas and names including polyatomic ions
lattice model, conductivity, solubility and volatility
qualitative lattice-strength comparison from ionic charge and radius
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Required polyatomic ions: NH4+, OH-, NO3-, HCO3-, CO3^2-, SO4^2-, PO4^3-.
Qualitative lattice enthalpy is shared; Born-Haber calculations are R1.2 HL.

topics.title: The covalent model
slConcepts: VSEPR with at most four central electron domains
network covalent solids and carbon allotropes
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Transition-metal complexes are HL even in coordination-bond examples.
No d-orbital hybridization classification is required.
Locating agents and operating details of GC/HPLC are excluded.
Distinguish electron-domain geometry from molecular geometry.

topics.title: The metallic model
slConcepts: metal cation/electron model and physical properties
s/p-metal bond strength and melting trends
additionalHlConcepts: delocalized d electrons and transition-metal properties
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Keep trend explanations in terms of charge, ion size and electron density.

topics.title: From models to materials
slConcepts: bonding continuum and electronegativity bonding triangle
polymer properties and addition repeating units
additionalHlConcepts: condensation repeating units of polyesters and polyamides
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Percentage ionic character calculations are excluded.
Specific alloy recipes and memorized monomer structures are not required.
Do not treat polyester/polyamide condensation as SL.

topics.title: The periodic table: Classification of elements
slConcepts: radius, ionization energy, electron affinity and electronegativity trends
group 1 with water and group 17 displacement
oxide acid/base trends and environmental effects
additionalHlConcepts: ionization-energy discontinuities explained using sublevel energy and pairing
transition-metal properties and first-row ion configurations
complex-ion colour from d splitting and complementary light
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Magnetism subtype detail and coordination-number splitting patterns are excluded.
Do not explain IE anomalies solely by a slogan about special stability.

topics.title: Functional groups: Classification of organic compounds
slConcepts: molecular, empirical, structural and skeletal representations
functional group identification and homologous series
IUPAC naming with up to six parent-chain carbons and one functional-group type
additionalHlConcepts: proton NMR environments, shifts, integrals and simple splitting
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Use hydroxy for the functional group; hydroxyl refers to the radical.
Naming covers saturated or mono-unsaturated chains, branching, and mono/di/tri/tetra/penta/hexa prefixes.
E-Z naming is excluded.
Cis-trans scope: non-cyclic alkenes and C3/C4 cycloalkanes.
NMR splitting scope: singlets, doublets, triplets and quartets.
Use wedge/dash for enantiomers; no R/S assignment required by these statements.

topics.title: Measuring enthalpy changes
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Use reaction coordinate and potential energy on energy-profile axes.
Account for heat loss, absorbed heat and reacting moles.

topics.title: Energy cycles in reactions
additionalHlConcepts: standard formation and combustion definitions and sums
Born-Haber energy accounting with singly/doubly charged ions
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Do not require construction of a complete Born-Haber cycle.
Give a clear lattice-formation versus lattice-dissociation sign convention.
Standard formation/combustion data sums are HL.

topics.title: Energy from fuels
slConcepts: fuel comparisons using carbon emissions and energy per mass
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Proton-exchange-membrane operation is excluded.
For fuel-cell half-equations specify acidic or alkaline electrolyte.

topics.title: Entropy and spontaneity
additionalHlConcepts: entropy distribution and standard entropy change
Gibbs energy and temperature dependence of spontaneity
non-standard Gibbs energy via reaction quotient
standard Gibbs energy and equilibrium constant
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Entire subtopic is HL.
Use consistent joules or kilojoules and absolute temperature.
Thermodynamic spontaneity is distinct from speed.

topics.title: How much? The amount of chemical change
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Percentage yield and atom economy quantify different things.

topics.title: How fast? The rate of chemical change
slConcepts: rates from concentration, mass or gas-volume data and tangents
concentration, pressure, surface area and temperature
additionalHlConcepts: elementary steps, intermediates and transition states
experimental orders, rate law and k units
Arrhenius analysis, including frequency/orientation factor A
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Do not assess detailed homogeneous/heterogeneous catalytic mechanisms.
Rate-determining step need not be first.
Rate law must be inferred from experimental or elementary-step evidence, not overall stoichiometry.

topics.title: How far? The extent of chemical change
slConcepts: dynamic equilibrium in a closed system
K magnitude, temperature dependence and reversing a reaction
qualitative Le Chatelier shifts including gas/aqueous equilibrium
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Quadratic equations are not expected.
Quantitative equilibrium-composition problems are HL.
Only homogeneous equilibria are assessed quantitatively here.

topics.title: Proton transfer reactions
additionalHlConcepts: buffer composition, action, pH and dilution
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Neutralization curves involve monoprotic acids/bases.
Quadratic solving is not expected.
Hydrated transition-metal-ion and aluminium-ion acidity is excluded.
Strong acid examples and concentration assumptions must be explicit when calculating pH.

topics.title: Electron transfer reactions
slConcepts: balanced half-equations in acidic or neutral solution
voltaic cells, salt bridge, rechargeable cells
additionalHlConcepts: standard hydrogen electrode and electrode potentials
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Do not require memorization of metal displacement series; provide evidence/data.
Specific organic oxidizing/reducing reagent names/formulas and their mechanisms are excluded.
Solvent/electrode/concentration complications need explicit controlled context.
No Faraday current-time electrolysis calculation statement appears in this syllabus.

topics.title: Electron sharing reactions
slConcepts: homolysis by UV/heat and single-electron arrows
alkane halogenation initiation, propagation and termination
multiple substitution products and alkane kinetic stability
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Entire subtopic is shared SL/HL.
Do not invent HL-only radical content to balance question counts.
Use radical dots and conserve atoms and radical count in each step.

topics.title: Electron-pair sharing reactions
slConcepts: alkene addition products for water, halogens and hydrogen halides
additionalHlConcepts: SN2 primary and SN1 tertiary mechanisms, secondary can use both
electrophilic addition mechanisms and carbocation stability
benzene electrophilic substitution with a supplied charged electrophile
scopeAndAuthoringNotes: Detailed substitution/addition mechanisms are not assessed at SL.
Solvent effects and comparison of mechanism-dependent rates are excluded.
Formation of the benzene-attacking electrophile is excluded.
Use curly arrows from a lone pair or bond to an atom/bond destination; never from a positive charge.
Show carbocation charges, required lone pairs, leaving-group charge and regeneration of catalyst where relevant.
